population_count_rule: NEOMOD2 Table 3 differential counts are reconstructed from each published cumulative low/central/high column. Missing mean is calculated separately for disjoint geometric categories after subtracting every catalogued object in the same H/orbit domain, including scientific holds. Nonnegative residuals and lower/upper per-bin envelopes are imposed; these branches are not draws from the unknown joint parameter posterior. No probability weights are assigned to branches. The current catalogue uses a later H calibration; no arbitrary discovery/magnitude recalibration is silently applied.
scope: Known asteroid catalogue in full, with nested all-albedo geometric pools and a separate Don Quixote exclusion. Inferred missing objects only for 15.25<=H<27.75, q<1.3 AU, a<4.2 AU, i<88 degrees. No main-belt inventory, Open Moon, planetary array or outer-system infrastructure is added. The all-NEA comparison is geological potential; the narrower geometric cuts are still not trajectories.
evidence: Conditional predictive Monte Carlo ranges under explicit observational, analogue and population assumptions. They are not empirically calibrated confidence limits, approved extractable stocks, route capability or project-success probabilities. The count model branches and common calibration/grade stress branches carry no probability weights.
albedo_bound_rule: Positive 0.005 lower truncation is an explicit numerical/physical prior limiting the unobserved ultra-dark tail, not an observed population minimum. Upper 1 is physical. Conditional p(albedo|H) weights the size-dependent NEOMOD3 Rayleigh distribution by its supplied differential log-diameter model, using quarter-magnitude lookup cells. Known taxonomy uses C/S component likelihoods. H<15 and H>28 imputation is extrapolation; measured diameter always takes precedence.
measurement_rule: Reported diameter sigma is used where supplied; a 20% standard-deviation scenario covers diameters lacking sigma. Reported albedos use an assumed log sigma ln1.4, motivated by cross-method scatter rather than an object-specific fit uncertainty. A common ±20% diameter calibration is separately stressed, never given a probability. Missing H and diameter produces an unquantified record, not zero geological mass.
composition_rule: MITHNEOS global debiased 42% S/Q and 48% carbonaceous fractions inform a broad prior; remaining 10% is ambiguous, not 10% metallic. Unknown groups are updated by C/S albedo likelihoods. X/ambiguous bodies take a metallic analogue with probability 0.125, midpoint of the cited 5–20% range; otherwise their C/stony ambiguity remains albedo-conditioned. Published classifications are not assigned to previously unknown objects in the catalogue evidence record. This is an explicit analogue model, not a published joint taxonomic posterior.
density_rule: Uniform per-object priors over Carry-derived ranges tabulated by USGS 2017 for stony, carbonaceous and metal-rich analogues. Neither measured density nor a confidence interval for each candidate is inferred.
grade_rule: Independent per-object random meteorite ranks use USGS 2017 Appendix 1/Figure 4 analogue fits for water equivalent and native iron, converting wt.% by dividing 100 and clipping nonnegative fractions so water+nativeiron<=bodymass. These are compositional potential, not extraction recovery. Mineral-bound hydrogen is reported as water equivalent; recoverability, energy and nitrogen are not inferred. Shared .5x/1.5x grade branches expose analogue calibration uncertainty.
numerical_rule: Individual catalogue bodies are sampled. Undiscovered categories use independent compound-Poisson counts under each fixed count branch; branch increments are coupled to guarantee monotonic total populations. Counts below 128 are explicitly summed. Larger sums use first and second compound moments estimated from 65536 synthetic bodies per H bin, with joint normal approximation and nonnegative physical projection. Conditional H within each half-magnitude count bin is uniform; this is a declared quadrature approximation. Source orbital cells are integrated as piecewise constant with 16-point Gauss quadrature. No replenishment from main-belt sources is credited over 220 years.
